newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen rangebound on diverse interest.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen rangebound on diverse interest.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on average volumes and ever-diversifying investor interest, traders said, seeing the market rangebound on Friday.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose slightly to close at 360.54, after 359.76 on Wednesday, on $36.6 million total market turnover. Healthy volume is considered to be around $40 million.
"There was decent interest in blue chips and second tiers, although the real interest is in all kinds of new sectors," said Viktor Pitaleff, head trader at Renaissance Capital.

Trade was also quiet on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), but regional power company Irkutskenergo was in demand, traders said, speculating it could be because banks barred from being shareholders could trade shares on MICEX.

The oil sector led the RTS top tier of liquid shares, with LUKoil LKOH.RTS , who forecast net profit by Russian cash accounting standards would grow to 4.0-4.5 trillion in 1997 from 3.8 trillion in 1996, rising to $15.45 from $15.30.
But national utility UES EESR.RTS slipped to $0.3135 from $0.3156. Natural gas producer Gazprom GAZP.RTS firmed slightly to $0.592 from $0.588.
Traders said new foreign funds which buoyed leading share prices on Wednesday was already being rechannelled to less liquid chemical, food-processing and defence sector shares.

"I see new money from the West but the money quickly goes to the second tier, which is very wide and voluminous and where capitalisation is growing not daily but hourly," said head trader at Rossiisky Kredit Bank Yevgeny Skibitsky.
"There's a widening of interest on securities due to their big growth potential. Because of that, the blue chips look less attractive."
Traders said the market would see domestic support at current levels but were wary of predicting a rise in prices.
"Everything seems to be at or near historic highs," said Renaissance's Pitaleff. "I wouldn't be so bold as to say I expect futher growth -- I think things could quiet down."
